memory_candidates.content: pytest's --import-mode=importlib resolves a collected package (e.g. 'tests.cli.foo') via direct sys.modules population during collection, not via a sys.path search -- so a submodule import like 'from tests.utils.helpers import X' inside a test body succeeds even when the package's root directory never appears anywhere in sys.path. Purging sys.path entries to prevent a different package (e.g. an installed library's source tree) from shadowing does not break this, since it operates through a completely separate resolution mechanism.

On this NixOS host, rootless podman works fine via `nix run nixpkgs#podman` without any setuid newuidmap wrapper -- the only blockers were two missing config files, ~/.config/containers/policy.json ({"default": [{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"}]}) and registries.conf (unqualified-search-registries = ["docker.io"]). A prior assumption that ad hoc podman requires host setuid wrapper support should be re-verified before being treated as a hard blocker.

This host's pip.conf sets install.user=true globally, which breaks `python -m build`'s isolated build-env creation with 'Can not perform a --user install' errors. Workaround: PIP_USER=0 python -m build.
